title: The source norm of a target pullback is groupoid-invariant
statement:
Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Suppose morphisms $s,t:R\to U$, $e:U\to R$, $i:R\to R$ and $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ [def-pc-fibre-product] make $U(H)$ and $R(H)$ the objects and arrows of a groupoid, functorially in every test scheme $H$, with the indicated source, target, identity, inverse and composition. Assume $s,t$ are finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free], and put $\sigma=s^\sharp$, $\tau=t^\sharp:A\to B$ and $C=\{a\in A:\sigma(a)=\tau(a)\}$. For $b\in B$, let $N_\sigma(b)\in A$ be the norm section of [lem-pd-finite-locally-free-norm-charts]: on every affine open where $B$ via $\sigma$ is finite free it is the determinant of multiplication by $b$ [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant]. Then for every $f\in A$,
$$N_\sigma(\tau(f))\in C,$$
that is, $\sigma(N_\sigma(\tau(f)))=\tau(N_\sigma(\tau(f)))$. No constant-rank, reducedness or freeness of the arrow relation is assumed.
